title: GPU correctable error surge and recovery heuristics — notes & runbook draft
body:
Summary:

This note captures an on-call investigation and a runbook draft focused on handling short bursts (surges) of correctable GPU ECC errors that intermittently lead to driver instability (hangs) and occasional kernel-level panics. The goal is to define deterministic triage steps, automated mitigations, and longer-term experiments to identify root cause(s) when we observe 'CCE surge' patterns across a rack or fleet subset.

Context / why this is different from a single-card ECC event:
- We saw multiple cards in the same rack reporting bursts of correctable ECC counts within minutes. The error pattern often preceded a GPU driver process hang (NVRM) or a GPU driver reset. Reboots frequently cleared the symptoms temporarily, but the burst reappeared after 12–72h.
- Unlike slow accumulation of soft ECCs, these surges are high-rate and clustered (many corrections per minute) and correlate with increased job retry rates and occasional CUDA context losses.

Incident outline (example):
- 2026-06-07 02:13 UTC: Datadog alert: gpu.ecc.correctable_rate >= 50/min aggregated across rack-7 cluster (threshold 20/min).
- 02:15 UTC: On-call received secondary alert: gpu.driver.hang detected on node gpu-node-r7-11 (SIGTRAP from nvidia module).
- 02:18 UTC: Ops manually cordoned node, drained k8s pods, and forced driver unload/reload.
- 02:29 UTC: Node rejoined; errors dropped but resumed intermittently at 05:40 UTC at lower amplitude.
- Collected logs and saved to s3://redwood-logs/gpu-ecc/2026-06-07.tar.gz

Immediate observations from logs (high level):
- dmesg excerpts showed repeated NVRM messages: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus" interleaved with correctable ECC reports.
- nvidia-smi -q showed per-device Correctable Errors spiking by hundreds within a minute; ECC counters reset after driver reload.
- No consistent SMART disk errors or PSU alarms reported for the affected rack; BMC data showed small transient power rail spikes around the times of interest.
- NVLink link errors were observed on a subset of nodes; partner link negotiation retried multiple times in the kernel logs.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Transient power/voltage noise on GPU rails during high batch workloads causes momentary bit flips that are corrected (CCE), but at high rates the driver/firmware retries cause NVLink/PCIe negotiation issues and eventually a driver hang.
2) Driver firmware incompatibility interacting with particular microcode on the GPUs under a certain thermal cycling pattern. Driver 535.xx reported in logs on affected nodes.
3) Bad DIMM on motherboard causing memory bus noise that manifests as GPU ECC.
4) A particular workload pattern triggers pathological allocation/frees that surface a software-level race in the driver leading to hangs when ECC rates are high.

Runbook draft (for on-call):
- Trigger conditions (what alerts should start this workflow):
  - Aggregated correctable ECC rate > 30/min for a rack OR per-node correctable ECC rate > 20/min sustained for 5 minutes.
  - AND/OR gpu.driver.hang alert fired (NVRM Xid 31/79 patterns).

- Immediate triage steps (first 15 minutes):
  1) Identify affected nodes: query metric "gpu.ecc.correctable_rate" and list nodes > threshold.
  2) On each affected node, run (copy logs to central location first):
     - sudo nvidia-smi -q -d ECC > /tmp/gpu-ecc-$(hostname).txt
     - sudo dmesg --ctime | egrep -i "NVRM|nvlink|ecc|Xid" | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg-nvidia-$(hostname).txt
     - sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 > /tmp/kubelet-tail.txt
     - sudo /usr/bin/nvidia-bug-report.sh --allow-origin > /tmp/nvidia-bug-$(hostname).tar.gz (collect and upload to S3)
  3) If the node shows driver hang symptoms (process respawn, stuck GPU): cordon the node and drain non-critical pods (kubectl cordon/drain --ignore-daemonsets).
  4) Attempt controlled driver unload/load: 
     - sudo systemctl stop kubelet && sudo rmmod nvidia_uvm nvidia_drm nvidia || true; sudo modprobe nvidia; sudo systemctl start kubelet
     - Note: only do this on nodes not critical for active training jobs; prefer evicting jobs first.
  5) If the node recovers and ECC counts drop, leave cordon for 30m and monitor for recurrence.
  6) If node cannot recover or kernel panics recur, open a hardware ticket and schedule immediate replacement/reimage.

- Automated mitigations (suggested):
  - Datadog monitor: when aggregated rack ECC rate > 30/min, auto-cordon nodes with per-node ECC > 20/min.
  - Short-circuit policy: if node has > 3 driver unloads in 24h due to ECC events, automatically retire the node to a diagnostic pool.
  - Expose a metric "gpu.ecc.correctable_burst" (max per-minute spike) to detect bursts vs slow accumulation.

- Diagnostic commands and log pointers (for postmortem):
  - nvidia-smi -q -d ECC; nvidia-smi --query-gpu=ecc.errors.corrected --format=csv
  - dmesg | egrep -i "NVRM|Xid|nvlink|ecc"
  - journalctl -k | egrep -i "PCIe|nvlink|nvidia"
  - ipmitool sdr elist to fetch BMC sensor logs around incident time
  - collect firmware versions: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,gpu_name,serial --format=csv
  - gather environmental telemetry (BMC, PDU logs, room temperature) for 1h before/after surge.

- Short experiments to run (follow-up, assign to hardware/sre):
  1) Reproduce under controlled stress: run memtest-like GPU kernel that allocates large tensor slices and toggles high-frequency kernel launches to see if ECC rate rises. Compare on affected node vs a control node.
  2) Swap PCIe riser / power cables and run overnight soak; monitor for reappearance.
  3) Temporarily roll back/up driver versions on a small pool (535.x -> 540.x or test older 525.x) to test driver/firmware interplay.
  4) Insert NVLink stress test between peer cards (if applicable) to exercise link negotiation path.

- Longer-term mitigations / proposals:
  - Add ECC-burst detection and automated evacuation policy (k8s label + autoscaler integration).
  - Formalize a hardware diagnostic workflow: isolate node, boot a minimal diagnostic image, run vendor memtests, capture BMC voltage traces.
  - Engage vendor (GPU OEM) with collected bugreports, dmesg excerpts, and BMC traces for firmware microcode analysis.
  - Improve lab reproducibility: maintain a small rack with identical firmware and power infrastructure for reproduction.

Open action items (owners assigned):
- Asha: Draft Datadog monitors for burst detection and automated cordon playbook (ETA: 2026-06-14).
- Marcus: Prepare a diagnostic image and checklist for hardware bench tests; schedule slot with lab (ETA: 2026-06-18).
- Sonia: Run driver version A/B tests on two spare nodes, collect metrics for 48h (ETA: 2026-06-20).
- Ethan: Correlate BMC/room-temps/power-logs with ECC events from historical data (past 6 months) and produce a short correlation report (ETA: 2026-06-17).

Notes for postmortem structure (if this escalates):
- Timeline with precise metric deltas and per-device ECC counters.
- Root cause hypothesis with evidence matrix (logs, BMC, firmware versions, workload samples).
- Why we missed it earlier (alert thresholds, telemetry gaps).
- Corrective and preventive actions (short/medium/long term) and owners.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Are we seeing any pattern with specific GPU serial ranges? (need inventory mapping).
- Do NVLink peer pairings correlate (same peer across multiple nodes showing errors)?
- Is there a subtle kernel/driver race triggered only under concurrent autoconfiguration of NVLink and heavy ECC corrections?

Appendix — quick symptom checklist for on-call (one-pager):
- Symptom: sudden spike in gpu.ecc.correctable_rate OR NVRM Xid 31/79 logs.
- Immediate: collect nvidia-bug-report, cordon, drain low-priority pods.
- If driver unload/load fixes -> leave cordoned and monitor 30m.
- If recurrence or kernel panic -> hardware ticket + replace node to diagnostic pool.

This doc is intended to be a working draft. Please add reproducer snippets, additional log excerpts, or corrections below.

(End of note)
